subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled producer/prompt that emits stale CORE.md and directory paths, or should OpenClaw change the generic read tool contract to soft-handle directory reads and related memory paths?
rationale: Source proves partial fixes and a remaining generic EISDIR shape, but the correct boundary depends on whether maintainers want producer-specific repair or a broader model-facing tool behavior change.

options.title: Fix the producer after live repro
options.body: Reproduce the current scheduled run with stability diagnostics and repair the cron/heartbeat or memory prompt path that asks for stale or directory targets.

options.title: Change read-tool semantics
options.body: Make read return a directory listing or soft result for directory paths, accepting the broader compatibility and model-contract change.

options.title: Narrow to daily-memory PR only
options.body: Treat the bare-date slice as covered by the existing related PR and keep this issue waiting only for separate CORE.md/RSS evidence.

recommendation.title: Fix the producer after live repro
recommendation.body: Reproduce the current scheduled run with stability diagnostics and repair the cron/heartbeat or memory prompt path that asks for stale or directory targets.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans cron scheduling, read-tool behavior, and heartbeat scheduling, which are the three remaining decision surfaces.
